rationale: Standard Coptic ⲁⲣⲓⲕⲉ from ⲁⲣⲓⲕⲉ 'find fault, blame, complain.' Used as the verbal action of the catechumen approaching the Elect — 'made complaint to.' Documents the catechumen's role as one who voices doubt/objection to the apostle.

proposed_english: who has lived / who is alive
rationale: Relative perfect on Lyc ⲟⲛ (= ⲱⲛϩ 'live'). Chapter title designating the long-lived/aging catechumen who complains about not yet being released.
Lyc verbal noun on ⲃⲱⲗ-family meaning 'release, dismissal' — soteriological release from the body for the righteous. Parallel to ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release' (in glossary) but with -ⲕ extension.

Title/name applied to the apostle in line 5, confirmed in line 17 to be the Illuminator (= Mani). Possible alternative analyses: corrupted Greek ἀρχαῖος 'Ancient (one)' as honorific epithet; or a personal name reflecting Mani's father Patikios. Preserved as proper name pending parallels.
Future verb in 'one shall harm another.' Possibly Lyc reflex of ϩⲱⲩϣ 'press, oppress' or related harm-verb. The verb of inter-elect violence the catechumen finds inexplicable.
Verb of malodorousness paralleled with ⲥϯⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ 'fragrance' on this page. The tree both stinks (in its smoke) and is fragrant (in its scent) — the dual quality grounding the parable.

On this page (line 30) ⲡⲕⲣⲙⲉⲥ pairs with ⲡⲕⲁⲡⲛⲟⲥ 'smoke' as the residue/byproduct doublet. Already in glossary as 'smoke' but here the doublet construction with κάπνος suggests differentiation: ⲕⲁⲡⲛⲟⲥ = airy smoke, ⲕⲣⲙⲉⲥ = sooty deposit. Refining glossary entry.
Verb in line 25 'if a man ⲟⲱⲣⲃⲉ of one (branch).' Etymology unclear; possibly Lyc form of ⲱⲣⲃ̄/ⲟⲩⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'pluck, send' or related. Tentative; flagged for parallels.
